standard_prerequisites.name: Induction principle of n-truncation
standard_prerequisites.statement: A section of a family of n-types over trunc n A is determined by its values on |a|_n.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is used repeatedly at source lines 637 and 645-648 to define maps and homotopies on truncated elements.

standard_prerequisites.name: Quasi-inverses give equivalences
standard_prerequisites.statement: A map with a two-sided homotopy inverse is an equivalence.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof builds phi and psi with homotopies H and K and concludes the equivalence from them at source lines 643-644.

core_obligations: Construct phi : Trunc n (Sigma x:A, Trunc n P(x)) -> Trunc n (Sigma x:A, P(x)) by induction on the truncation, setting phi(|(x,|u|_n)|_n) := |(x,u)|_n (source lines 639-640 and 645).
Construct psi in the opposite direction, setting psi(|(x,u)|_n) := |(x,|u|_n)|_n (source lines 641-642 and 646).
Define the homotopies H : phi o psi ~ id and K : psi o phi ~ id by induction on the truncation, both given by refl at the displayed generators (source lines 643-644 and 647-648).
Conclude that phi and psi are quasi-inverses and hence that the induced map between the truncations is an equivalence (source lines 643-644).

proof_roadmap.step: Announce the plan: build two maps by repeated truncation induction and exhibit them as quasi-inverses.
Define phi and psi on the generators.
Define the two homotopies and conclude the equivalence.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Theorem 7.3.9 at source lines 629-634: for any family P : A -> type, trunc n (Sigma x:A, trunc n P(x)) is equivalent to trunc n (Sigma x:A, P(x)). The proof (source lines 636-649) is a complete quasi-inverse construction, not a citation: both directions have to be defined by induction on the n-truncation (source lines 645-646), which requires the induction principle to be applied to the family of n-types in question, and the two homotopies are then given by a second and third application of the same principle, with refl at the generators (source lines 647-648). Only after phi, psi, H and K are all in place does the equivalence follow. The statement records none of the four objects that have to be built.
